questions.question: Explain the chain of causes and consequences of rural depopulation, and give two strategies used to address it.
questions.expected_answer: Push factors such as drought, farm mechanisation shedding labour, land degradation and poor services drive people out, while pull factors like jobs, schools and hospitals draw them to cities. As the young and skilled leave first, the rural population ages, schools and clinics close as numbers fall, farm labour becomes scarce, and local businesses fail because their threshold populations disappear. Strategies include rural development programmes and agri-processing to create jobs, improved services and infrastructure, and land reform through restitution, redistribution and tenure reform.

questions.question: Describe the structure of the South African city model and explain how its apartheid origins create today's urban issues.
questions.expected_answer: The South African city has a CBD at the core with formerly white suburbs close to central amenities, a transition zone of older mixed land use, and townships and informal settlements pushed to the far periphery, separated from the rest of the city by buffer zones of open land. Because homes were deliberately placed far from workplaces, residents face long, expensive commutes, while the periphery carries housing shortages, service backlogs and growing informal settlements. Responses include in-situ upgrading of informal settlements, public transport investment such as bus rapid transit, and inner-city renewal.

questions.question: Name South Africa's four core industrial regions and explain the difference between an Industrial Development Zone and a Spatial Development Initiative, with one example of each.
questions.expected_answer: The four core regions are Gauteng (the PWV), Durban-Pinetown, Port Elizabeth-Uitenhage and the South-western Cape. An IDZ is a purpose-built industrial estate linked to a port or airport, designed to attract export-oriented manufacturing, for example Coega near Gqeberha. An SDI is a corridor of coordinated investment linking regions to unlock economic potential, for example the Maputo Corridor linking Gauteng to the port of Maputo.
